([[Indianapolis|Indianapolis, Indiana]]) | college = * [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State]] (2019–2021) * [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]] (2021–2022) | highlights = * Second-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2022) * Second-team All-[[Missouri Valley Conference|MVC]] (2021) * MVC All-Newcomer Team (2020) * MVC All-Freshman Team (2020) }} '''Jacob LaRavia''' (born November 3, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]] and the [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State Sycamores]]. ==Early life and high school career== LaRavia is the son of Jeff and Becky LaRavia. His family moved from [[Pasadena, California]] to [[Indianapolis]] when LaRavia was six years old. LaRavia played basketball for [[Lawrence Central High School]] in Indianapolis, where he was teammates with [[Nijel Pack]] and D'Andre Davis. He had a limited role until his senior season, in which he became the team's leading scorer.{{cite web |last1=Neddenriep |first1=Kyle |title=Jake LaRavia's breakout year a big reason No. 2 Lawrence Central has state title aspirations |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/03/07/siu-edwardsville-recruit-jake-laravia-leads-way-lawrence-central/3090800002/ |website=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |access-date=June 12, 2022 |date=March 7, 2019}} As a senior, LaRavia averaged 17.3 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 2.3 steals per game, earning Indiana All-Star honors. He helped Lawrence Central win its first sectional title since 2012. LaRavia first committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[SIU Edwardsville Cougars men's basketball|SIU Edwardsville]] but reopened his recruitment after a coaching change. He later committed to [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State]].{{cite web |last1=Neddenriep |first1=Kyle |title=Lawrence Central's Jake LaRavia commits to Indiana State |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/04/14/basketball-recruiting-jake-laravia-commits-indiana-state-sycamores/3465001002/ |website=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |access-date=June 12, 2022 |date=April 14, 2019}} ==College career== As a freshman at Indiana State, LaRavia averaged 9.4 points and 5.9 rebounds per game. He was named to the All-Newcomer and All-Freshman Teams in the [[Missouri Valley Conference]] (MVC).{{cite web |title=Key and LaRavia Named Preseason All-Missouri Valley Conference; Sycamores Picked Fourth in MVC Preseason Poll |url=https://gosycamores.com/news/2020/10/14/basketball-key-and-laravia-named-preseason-all-missouri-valley-conference-sycamores-picked-fourth-in-mvc-preseason-poll |publisher=Indiana State University Athletics |access-date=June 12, 2022 |date=October 15, 2020}} In his sophomore season, LaRavia averaged 12.3 points and 6.3 rebounds per game, earning second-team All-MVC recognition. Following the departure of coach [[Greg Lansing]], he transferred to [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]].{{cite web |last1=Gordon |first1=Todd Aaron |title=LaRavia era at ISU is over as forward commits to Wake Forest |url=https://www.tribstar.com/laravia-era-at-isu-is-over-as-forward-commits-to-wake-forest/article_d0d95e1d-ade6-5fe9-8a33-23bd2d0c0122.html |website=[[Tribune-Star]] |access-date=June 12, 2022 |date=March 16, 2021}} On January 22, 2022, LaRavia recorded a career-high 31 points, 10 rebounds and four assists in a 98–76 win against [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].{{cite web |title=Jake LaRavia scores 31 as Wake Forest beats North Carolina 98-76 |url=https://www.wfmynews2.com/article/sports/jake-laravia-scores-31-as-wake-forest-beats-north-carolina-98-76/83-ff81c76d-6359-4be8-8a24-fccb260dc1df |publisher=[[WFMY-TV]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=June 12, 2022 |date=January 23, 2022}} He averaged 14.6 points, 6.6 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game as a junior. He was named to the second-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]].{{cite web |last1=Taylor |first1=Cody |title=Wake Forest junior Jake LaRavia invited to NBA draft combine |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/05/04/wake-forest-jake-laravia-nba-draft-combine/ |publisher=The Rookie Wire |access-date=June 12, 2022 |date=May 4, 2022}} On June 1, 2022, LaRavia announced that he would remain in the [[2022 NBA draft]] and forgo his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Taylor |first1=Cody |title=Potential first-round pick Jake LaRavia to remain in NBA draft |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/06/01/wake-forest-jake-laravia-nba-draft-agent/ |publisher=The Rookie Wire |access-date=June 12, 2022 |date=June 1, 2022}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://gosycamores.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jake-laravia/6070 Indiana State Sycamores bio] *[https://godeacs.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jake-laravia/6353 Wake Forest Demon Deacons bio] [[Category:2001 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Indianapolis]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]] [[Category:Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball players]] [[Category:Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball players]]
